name: Diest, c. 1650
attribution: Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); historical land cover, town walls and gates from the Ferraris map (1777) and the Villaret map (1745-48), Digitaal Vlaanderen (geo.api.vlaanderen.be/HISTCART)

gateSources.Schaluinpoort: inventory 140037 (S2 in docs/research/history-check.md): Schaluinpoort, towards Antwerp and the Kempen; 'Antwerpsepoort' is the Ferraris (1770s) name
gateSources.Beverenpoort: inventory 140037: Beverenpoort, towards Hasselt and Maastricht; 'Maastrichtsepoort' is the Ferraris (1770s) name
gateSources.Putterstraatpoort: inventory 140037: Putterstraatpoort, towards Leuven and Aarschot; 'Leuvensepoort' is the Ferraris (1770s) name
gateSources.Koepoort: inventory 140037: one of five small gates walled up after 1508 - NOT a working gate in 1650
gateSources.Demerpoort: not in the inventory list; the Demer's passage through the wall, name unverified

walls.note: Diest town wall, unchanged between c.1560 and 1650; copied from tools/history/walls_1560.json (traced from the Ferraris map, 1777). Local metres around the Grote Markt (x east, z south). Gate names of the 14th-c. enceinte (Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed 140037), replacing the Ferraris (1770s) names used earlier; see docs/research/history-check.md F63.

landmarks.y1650: Main church with the unfinished west tower; the crossing tower ('de Mosterdpot') got its carillon only in 1671.

landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Diest' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140037)

landmarks.y1650: The medieval schepenhuis (1337); the present town hall dates from the 1720s.

landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Diest' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140037)

landmarks.y1650: Residence of the Nassau lords of Diest from 1499.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Diest' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140037)

ruler.note: Barony of the House of Orange-Nassau within Spanish Brabant
ruler.name: Hertogdom Brabant
ruler.sovereign: Philip IV of Spain, as duke (Spanish Netherlands); governor Archduke Leopold Wilhelm 1647-56
ruler.source: nl.wikipedia 'Hertogdom Brabant'; Vrede van Munster (1648); inventory 140194 (Halen); docs/research/history-check.md F31 (governor)
